questions.question: When is a random variable called discrete?
options: When it can take every real value in an interval.
When its set of possible values is finite or countably infinite
When it is not a function
questions.explanation: A random variable is discrete when its set of possible values is finite or countably infinite (e.g. $\{0,1,2,\ldots\}$).

questions.question: How are event probabilities computed for a discrete random variable?
questions.explanation: For a discrete variable, $P(X\in A)=\sum_{x\in A}p_X(x)$: sum the masses of the values in the event $A$.
